input.text: This is Houhai — "the Back Sea" — where old Beijing comes out to play at night. One of the Shichahai lakes, Houhai spent centuries as an aristocratic playground: princes built their gardens here, opera barges floated on summer nights. Today the tradition continues in modern costume: the south and east shores glow with lantern-lit bars and live music venues, while just one hutong back, families play chess under the willows as if the neon didn't exist. That contrast is the magic of Houhai — and your evening plan writes itself. At dusk, walk the shore from the Yinding Bridge: swans and pedal boats at golden hour, then music rising as the lights come on. In winter the lake freezes solid and becomes Beijing's great ice playground — sledges, skates, and sixty-year-old hockey games. Come for a drink, stay for the people-watching — Houhai is where Beijing's daytime shyness ends.
